content: Estriol, also known as oestriol, is one of the three primary estrogens produced by the human body. It is produced in significant amounts only during pregnancy, as it is synthesized by the placenta. Research conducted at UCLA's Geffen Medical School has shown that in pregnant women with multiple sclerosis (MS), estriol can significantly reduce the symptoms of the disease. In non-pregnant women, estriol levels do not fluctuate significantly after menopause and are comparable to the levels found in men. Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S), which is produced by the fetal adrenal cortex, is converted into estriol by the placenta. If a pregnant woman has abnormally low levels of unconjugated estriol, it may indicate potential developmental issues in the fetus.
